html:
The Nlaka'pamux, long called the Thompson, are an Interior Salish people of southern British Columbia, along the Fraser River canyon and the lower Thompson River. The map places them near the coast, a little south of their real homeland.

They lived from the great salmon runs, dried fish for winter, and traded fish and other goods between the coast and the interior plateau. In 1808 the fur trader Simon Fraser came down the river through their canyon, and the Thompson River was later named after his partner David Thompson.

The Fraser Canyon Gold Rush of 1858 brought thousands of miners into their land and led to a short war with them. Today the Nlaka'pamux form several First Nations bands. See also Nlaka'pamux on the modern map, and the wider Pacific fishing peoples.
